title: Your ITR Filing Checklist: A Month-Wise Guide for Salaried Taxpayers
description: Proactive tax planning throughout the year can significantly simplify your Income Tax Return (ITR) filing process. Begin by understanding your current tax sit.

faq.q: What is the difference between AIS and Form 26AS?
faq.a: AIS (Annual Information Statement) is a comprehensive view of all financial transactions reported against your PAN, including high-value transactions. Form 26AS primarily focuses on tax credits like TDS, TCS, and advance tax paid. AIS is more detailed and covers a broader range of information.

faq.q: Can I change my tax regime choice after informing my employer?
faq.a: Yes, for salaried individuals, the choice of tax regime (old or new) declared to the employer for TDS purposes is provisional. You can make the final choice at the time of filing your Income Tax Return.

faq.q: What if there's a mismatch between my Form 16 and Form 26AS/AIS?
faq.a: If you find a discrepancy, first contact your employer or the respective deductor (e.g., bank for interest) to get it rectified. If it's a significant issue, you might need to approach the Income Tax Department for clarification or correction.

faq.q: How long should I keep my tax-related documents?
faq.a: It is generally recommended to retain tax-related documents for at least 7-8 assessment years from the end of the relevant assessment year. This is because the Income Tax Department can reopen assessments for up to 7 years in certain cases.

faq.q: Is it mandatory to file ITR even if my tax is fully deducted at source?
faq.a: Yes, if your gross total income exceeds the basic exemption limit, filing an ITR is mandatory, even if all your tax has been deducted at source. Filing ITR also helps claim refunds, carry forward losses, and is often required for loan applications or visa processing.

faq.q: What is the basic exemption limit for salaried individuals?
faq.a: For individuals below 60 years of age, the basic exemption limit is ₹2.5 lakhs under the old tax regime. Under the new tax regime (default from FY 2023-24), the basic exemption limit is ₹3 lakhs.

faq.q: Do I need to report exempt income in my ITR?
faq.a: Yes, even exempt income (like agricultural income or certain allowances) should be reported in your ITR, although it won't be subject to tax. This provides a complete picture of your financial inflows to the tax authorities.
